newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes higher on Sparks estimate, soy.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes higher on Sparks estimate, soy.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on trade talk Sparks Companies pegged 1997 U.S. corn production at 9.48 billion bushels and on a rally in nearby soybeans, traders said.
That tally is below USDA's current outlook for 9.84 billion and below some other private forecasts for up to 10.0 billion bushels.
"The (Sparks) corn number is pretty low considering how well everything looks," said Ron Kucha, CBOT floor broker for O'Connor and Co.
The Memphis-based analytical firm also estimated 1997 U.S. soybean production at 2.68 billion bushels, above USDA's present outlook for 2.6 billion, traders said.
Sparks officials were unavailable for comment on the estimates.
Corn futures also rallied because they were oversold and due for a correction, sources said.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for July fell below 19 percent by Monday's close. An RSI of 30 or less is considered an oversold market.
Corn closed steady to 3-1/2 cents a bushel higher, with July up 2-3/4 at $2.43-1/4. December ended up 1/2 at $2.29-3/4.
Traders said there were no big surprises in Monday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report. But the commercial position in corn did garner some attention.
"The commercial long in corn is significant though and maybe is telling us we're getting a little too cheap (corn prices)," a trader said.
The CFTC said as of July 1, commercials were long corn by 756.5 million bushels and short by 373 million. Non-commercials were long corn by 137.9 million bushels and short by 304.2 million.
Monday's USDA condition rating for the U.S. corn crop was mildly supportive, the traders said.
USDA pegged the crop as of Sunday at 75 percent good to excellent, above the 74 percent a week ago but some traders were expecting up to an 80 percent good to excellent rating.
Funds bought at least 25.0 million bushels of corn, traders said. Refco Inc bought nine million December and Smith Barney bought seven million bushels of December, traders said.
ABN Amro-The Chicago Corp sold 10.0 million bushels of December and sold 3.5 million bushels of March, traders said.
In spread trading, Rosenthal Collins did two million bushesl of December/July 1998 at 18 cents, premium July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 82,000 contracts, above the 71,718 traded Monday.

In corn options, Prudential Securities sold 1,000 September $2.20 puts at 2-1/4 to 2-1/8 cents, bought 900 September $2.70 calls at 1-1/4 cents, bought 800 September $2.40 calls at five cents and bought 800 September $2.50 calls at 3-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 22,000 contracts, below the 23,436 traded Monday.
